items.depicts: A large framed switchboard panel with a blue header bar and four vertical light-blue bays, each topped by a dark bezel with an animated green status light on the leftmost unit.

proposals.name: Peering Exchange
proposals.why: Directly names the multi-bay colocation switchboard where autonomous networks interconnect.

proposals.name: Meet-Me Room
proposals.why: Uses the dry colocation industry term for the physical hall where competing carriers cross-connect.

proposals.name: Peering Rookery
proposals.why: Treats the towering bank of bays like a crowded cliffside nesting ground for backbone links.

items.recommendWhy: Meet-Me Room is authentic telecom jargon that reads as quietly funny in a field manual without trying too hard.
items.decisionWhy: This is the signature landmark anchor for the Internet / BGP layer and deserves its own full manual page.

items.depicts: A dark-framed card displaying a blue header block, a dark label bar, a gray rule, and an animated green-and-amber segmented bar along the bottom.
items.concept: BGP routing tables and prefix announcements

proposals.name: Route Table
proposals.why: Clearly identifies the card as a live table of network prefixes and path states.

proposals.name: Route Flap Board
proposals.why: Nods to BGP route flapping, where unstable prefixes oscillate between green and amber states.

proposals.name: Border Almanac
proposals.why: Frames the routing ledger as a naturalist's reference book tracking shifting frontier paths.

items.recommendWhy: Route Flap Board ties the animated status bar directly to one of BGP's most notorious failure modes.
items.decisionWhy: Distinct animated prop representing the defining protocol of this layer.

items.depicts: A horizontal two-tone blue-and-navy conduit banded at regular intervals by four amber collars, resembling an armored undersea cable.

proposals.name: Submarine Cable
proposals.why: States plainly what the armored banded trunk represents in global internet infrastructure.

proposals.name: Backhoe Bait
proposals.why: References the classic operations maxim that buried and coastal fiber trunks inevitably attract excavation equipment.

proposals.name: Abyssal Trunkline
proposals.why: Evokes the deep-ocean benthic habitat of transoceanic cables in a field-guide register.

items.recommendWhy: Abyssal Trunkline fits the binder's dry naturalist tone while remaining immediately recognizable as a submarine cable.
items.decisionWhy: Unique art with strong visual identity and rich real-world infrastructure lore.

items.depicts: A white index card with a green header strip, a navy drop shadow, and three horizontal bars representing resolved record fields.

proposals.name: DNS Record
proposals.why: Plainly labels the index card as a single resource record from a zone file.

proposals.name: It Was DNS
proposals.why: Cites the perennial sysadmin postmortem conclusion blamed for nearly every unexplained outage.

proposals.name: Resolver Ledger
proposals.why: Casts the small ruled card as an archival slip consulted whenever a name must be translated.

items.recommendWhy: Resolver Ledger suits an archival manual page title cleanly while leaving room for the DNS-outage joke in the BUGS section.
items.decisionWhy: Core internet primitive with dedicated sprite art and ample material for a manual entry.

items.depicts: A white pixelated cloud with a blue rectangular badge across its center and a pale blue shadow beneath it.

proposals.name: Autonomous Cloud
proposals.why: Directly pairs the cloud silhouette with the concept of an autonomous routing domain.

proposals.name: Bogon Cloud
proposals.why: References bogons, the unallocated or reserved address blocks that should never appear in global routing tables.

proposals.name: Sovereign Cumulus
proposals.why: Describes a self-governing network domain as a distinct cloud species in a field guide.

items.recommendWhy: Autonomous Cloud is immediately intelligible and already carries a dry deadpan humor on its own.
items.decisionWhy: Distinct sprite representing the organizational unit of internet routing.

items.depicts: A thin horizontal cyan optical line with a bright white light pulse traveling at its right tip.

proposals.name: Optical Fiber
proposals.why: Directly describes the glowing cyan glass strand carrying light pulses.

proposals.name: Dark Fiber
proposals.why: Plays ironically on the telecom term for unlit leased fiber, even as a pulse runs down this strand.

proposals.name: Glass Filament
proposals.why: Treats the slender optical link like a delicate physical specimen under a magnifying glass.

items.recommendWhy: Glass Filament captures the minimal visual form cleanly in the field-manual register.
items.decisionWhy: The sprite is a minimal animated horizontal line that works best as an appendix specimen rather than a full page.

items.depicts: A dark navy box with a cream front panel, four alternating amber and green LEDs, and two upright dark gray antennas.

proposals.name: Edge Router
proposals.why: Plainly identifies the dual-antenna forwarding appliance at the network boundary.

proposals.name: Default Gateway
proposals.why: References the catch-all 0.0.0.0/0 hop where every unresolved packet gets dumped.

proposals.name: Twin-Horn Relay
proposals.why: Describes the twin-antenna silhouette as if cataloging a horned mechanical beetle.

items.recommendWhy: Default Gateway is instantly recognizable computing vocabulary with a dry, bureaucratic ring.
items.decisionWhy: Clear, readable custom sprite representing a foundational networking device.

items.depicts: A dark gray pedestal supporting a tilted pale-blue parabolic dish with a darker blue feed horn angled toward the lower right.

proposals.name: Uplink Dish
proposals.why: Directly names the parabolic transceiver mounted on its pedestal.

proposals.name: High-Latency Ear
proposals.why: Pokes dryly at the unavoidable round-trip delay of geostationary satellite links.

proposals.name: Skyward Paraboloid
proposals.why: Uses crisp geometric field-guide language suited to a technical archive binder.

items.recommendWhy: Uplink Dish is concise, unmistakable, and lets the manual entry unpack satellite latency in prose.
items.decisionWhy: Distinct silhouette and unique internet-layer infrastructure prop.

items.depicts: A white envelope-like card with a cyan top header bar, a navy drop shadow, a gray address line, and an amber square payload block.

proposals.name: Network Packet
proposals.why: Plainly names the header-and-payload envelope moving across the wire.

proposals.name: Best-Effort Datagram
proposals.why: References IP's famously noncommittal delivery guarantee, which promises neither arrival nor order.

proposals.name: Stamped Dispatch
proposals.why: Evokes the postal metaphor of the envelope-and-stamp sprite in a dry archival voice.

items.recommendWhy: Best-Effort Datagram captures the exact protocol semantics with understated computing humor.
items.decisionWhy: Core networking abstraction with clean, unique sprite art.

items.depicts: A closed green padlock with a lighter green shackle and a vertical white keyhole slot in the center.

proposals.name: TLS Padlock
proposals.why: Directly identifies the green lock icon signaling an encrypted transport session.

proposals.name: Trust Anchor
proposals.why: Uses the dry PKI term for a root certificate while nodding to the fragile chain of trust behind the green lock.

proposals.name: Cipher Clasp
proposals.why: Frames the cryptographic seal as a physical fastener in the field-manual lexicon.

items.recommendWhy: Trust Anchor is authentic PKI terminology that sounds weightier and drier than a generic padlock.
items.decisionWhy: Distinct sprite not shared with userspace's padlock, covering transport encryption and certificates.

items.depicts: A small navy-bordered browser window with a tab strip, gray address bar, amber hero banner, and a muted line of body copy.

proposals.name: Browser Window
proposals.why: Plainly describes the miniature tabbed viewport.

proposals.name: Tab Hoarder
proposals.why: Wryly alludes to the universal habit of accumulating dozens of forgotten browser tabs.

proposals.name: Glass Viewport
proposals.why: Treats the framed window like an observation pane looking into the application layer.

items.recommendWhy: Browser Window is direct and avoids over-explaining a familiar UI landmark.
items.decisionWhy: Both sprite variants are byte-identical copies of e:app-browser from the application layer.

items.depicts: A cream modal window with an amber title bar, a red close button, an amber warning icon, two text bars, and two confirmation buttons.

proposals.name: Modal Dialog
proposals.why: Accurately names the blocking window demanding user acknowledgment.

proposals.name: Are You Sure
proposals.why: Quotes the reflexive confirmation prompt that users dismiss without reading.

proposals.name: Amber Interrupter
proposals.why: Describes the warning box like a bright-crowned specimen that halts all surrounding activity.

items.recommendWhy: Modal Dialog is precise UI terminology that fits the manual's formal register.
items.decisionWhy: Byte-identical duplicate of e:app-dialog reused in the internet layer.

items.depicts: A white notification card with a navy drop shadow, an amber icon square on the left, and two horizontal text bars.

proposals.name: Toast Banner
proposals.why: Plainly names the transient popup notification card.

proposals.name: Transient Nag
proposals.why: Dryly characterizes short-lived UI alerts that vanish just before you finish reading them.

proposals.name: Fleeting Notice
proposals.why: Casts the disappearing card as an ephemeral slip pinned briefly to the screen.

items.recommendWhy: Toast Banner uses the established UI term cleanly and unambiguously.
items.decisionWhy: Byte-identical duplicate of e:app-toast reused from the application layer.

items.depicts: A square cream tile containing an eight-dot ring of gray and amber squares that cycles as an indeterminate loading indicator.

proposals.name: Loading Spinner
proposals.why: Directly identifies the cycling eight-dot wait indicator.

proposals.name: Throbber of Doom
proposals.why: Revives the classic 1990s UI term throbber for an activity indicator that may never resolve.

proposals.name: Amber Orbit
proposals.why: Describes the circling dots as a miniature celestial loop in field-guide prose.

items.recommendWhy: Loading Spinner is clear and understated, matching the manual's plainspoken technical voice.
items.decisionWhy: Byte-identical duplicate of e:app-spinner reused from the application layer.

items.depicts: A horizontal navy-bordered cream trough with a small amber fill block near the left edge.

proposals.name: Progress Bar
proposals.why: Plainly labels the linear completion meter.

proposals.name: Ninety-Nine Percent
proposals.why: References the universal computing experience of progress bars stalling indefinitely at the final step.

proposals.name: Measured Trough
proposals.why: Describes the horizontal meter as a physical gauge channel.

items.recommendWhy: Ninety-Nine Percent is quietly funny and universally understood by anyone who has watched a transfer stall.
items.decisionWhy: Both sprite variants are byte-identical duplicates of e:app-progress from the application layer.

items.depicts: A small rounded green square tile with a white inner glyph and a bright red notification badge on its upper-right corner.
items.concept: app launcher icon with unread badge

proposals.name: App Tile
proposals.why: Plainly identifies the compact launcher icon.

proposals.name: Unread Badge
proposals.why: Focuses on the red corner dot engineered to trigger compulsive checking.

proposals.name: Red-Crowned Tile
proposals.why: Borrows ornithological naming conventions to describe the bright red mark on its corner.

items.recommendWhy: Unread Badge highlights the single most recognizable and psychologically fraught pixel on the sprite.
items.decisionWhy: Both sprite variants are byte-identical duplicates of e:app-icon from the application layer.

items.depicts: A blue speech bubble with a bottom-right tail and three animated typing-indicator dots inside.

proposals.name: Chat Bubble
proposals.why: Plainly names the speech-balloon messaging widget.

proposals.name: Is Typing
proposals.why: Captures the low-grade suspense of three animated dots that may never yield a message.

proposals.name: Blue Utterance
proposals.why: Treats the suspended speech balloon as an observed specimen of human chatter.

items.recommendWhy: Is Typing is a crisp, dry reference that turns a tiny three-dot animation into an immediate joke.
items.decisionWhy: Byte-identical duplicate of e:app-bubble reused from the application layer.

items.depicts: A white cloud silhouette with a blue T-shaped upload arrow centered above a pale blue shadow bar.

proposals.name: Cloud Sync
proposals.why: Plainly describes the cloud icon and animated upload arrow.

proposals.name: Someone Else's Disk
proposals.why: Echoes the classic dry reminder that cloud storage is merely another host's filesystem.

proposals.name: Uplink Nimbus
proposals.why: Combines telecom terminology with cloud taxonomy for a field-guide title.

items.recommendWhy: Cloud Sync is immediately clear and concise as a manual entry heading.
items.decisionWhy: Byte-identical duplicate of e:app-cloudsync reused from the application layer.

items.depicts: A golden-yellow file folder with a top-left index tab and a pale cream sheet peeking out of the opening.

proposals.name: File Folder
proposals.why: Plainly names the classic desktop directory icon.

proposals.name: Untitled Folder
proposals.why: Nods to the proliferating default-named directories cluttering every real desktop.

proposals.name: Manila Folio
proposals.why: Anchors the digital metaphor back to physical office stationery in the binder's archival voice.

items.recommendWhy: Untitled Folder is deadpan, authentic, and instantly recognizable to any computer user.
items.decisionWhy: Both sprite variants are byte-identical duplicates of e:app-folder from the application layer.

items.depicts: A slate-gray lidded wastebasket with three vertical ribs and a yellow scrap of paper sticking out under the lid.
items.concept: deferred file deletion and trash bin

proposals.name: Trash Bin
proposals.why: Plainly labels the ribbed desktop wastebasket.

proposals.name: Dev Null
proposals.why: References the Unix bit-bucket device where discarded output vanishes permanently.

proposals.name: Tin Receptacle
proposals.why: Describes the small gray bin as a dry catalog entry for an everyday artifact.

items.recommendWhy: Dev Null bridges desktop UI iconography with Unix manual-page literacy in two words.
items.decisionWhy: Byte-identical duplicate of e:app-trash reused from the application layer.

items.depicts: A horizontal bar filled amber on the left and gray on the right, bisected by a tall amber thumb with a white center.

proposals.name: Range Slider
proposals.why: Accurately names the horizontal value-selection widget.

proposals.name: Off-By-One Slider
proposals.why: References the frustrating precision of pixel-wide slider tracks that never land on the exact value you want.

proposals.name: Amber Detent
proposals.why: Treats the sliding thumb as a tactile mechanical stop in a field-guide register.

items.recommendWhy: Range Slider is clean, precise, and unambiguous.
items.decisionWhy: Byte-identical duplicate of e:app-slider reused from the application layer.

items.depicts: A tiny white flying bird with a blue head and beak and a two-pixel cyan contrail trailing behind it.

proposals.name: Packet Bird
proposals.why: Directly describes the small flying and perching courier native to the internet layer.

proposals.name: RFC 1149 Carrier
proposals.why: Cites the famous April Fools RFC specifying IP datagram transmission by homing pigeon.

proposals.name: Cyan-Tailed Swift
proposals.why: Names the critter like a genuine bird-guide species based on its blue-white plumage and cyan wake.

items.recommendWhy: RFC 1149 Carrier is a peak computing-literate reference that fits a flying internet critter effortlessly.
items.decisionWhy: Primary flying and perching critter species unique to the Internet / BGP layer.

proposals.why: Plainly identifies the miniature floating transceiver with twin blue panels.

proposals.name: Ping Probe
proposals.why: Nods to ICMP echo probes drifting across the network and blinking green when a host responds.

proposals.name: Green-Bellied Drifter
proposals.why: Catalogs the floating critter in classic naturalist field-guide style by its underside marking.

items.recommendWhy: Ping Probe is crisp, computing-literate, and pairs neatly with the green status pixel underneath.
